title: v1/chat.completions adapter: normalize params, stabilize streaming framing, structured tool-call envelope
author: Evelyn Chen
description: Motivation: Clients using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface exhibit divergent behavior around a few tricky corners: 1) parameter shapes (temperature, top_p, stop) inconsistent across SDKs and examples; 2) roles/tags mapping when system/user/assistant are missing or mis-ordered; 3) streaming framing sensitivity causing truncation of final tokens in some runtimes; 4) function/tool call payloads arriving as free-form text instead of a stable structured envelope; and 5) logprobs / stop interactions where logprobs are requested alongside various stop sequences. This PR implements a compatibility adapter and runtime fixes to make Redwood's hosted API behavior line up with common OpenAI expectations while keeping production safety and performance. Summary of changes: - Add an OpenAI compatibility adapter (src/api/openai_compat/chat_adapter.py) that:   * Normalizes scalar and array params: temperature (default 1.0), top_p (coerced between 0-1), presence_penalty/frequency_penalty fallbacks, and consistent precedence rules when both top_p and temperature are present.   * Canonicalizes stop: accepts string, array, null; converts to internal stop predicates; preserves empty-string and multi-byte separators. Adds safeguards to avoid accidental infinite-stop loops when stop tokens overlap with the model's tokenizer boundaries.   * Ensures logprobs requests are honored and mapped to internal scoring pipeline; if both logprobs and streaming are requested, we return per-token logprobs in the stream envelope (see streaming framing below). - Streaming framing stability (src/runtime/stream/framer.py):   * Introduce a framed streaming envelope with sequence id, partial_token boolean, and incremental token offsets to avoid ambiguous concatenation across TCP/HTTP chunk boundaries.   * Add a finalization handshake chunk (type: "done", seq: N) that guarantees client-side completion recognition even for long tail latency tokens.   * Add retry-safe idempotence metadata so clients that re-connect mid-stream can resume without duplicating output (the adapter will dedupe tokens with matching seq/offset ranges). - Structured tool/function calling envelope (pkg/protocol/structured_output.proto, src/api/openai_compat/tool_call_adapter.py):   * Tool invocations emitted as a structured object: { "tool_name": string, "arguments": { ... }, "metadata": { "invocation_id": uuid, "confidence": float } } instead of best-effort JSON in assistant message content.   * Backwards-compat shim: if a client expects plain assistant content, we also include a human-readable rendering under content["rendered"] while keeping the machine-parseable envelope in content["tool_call"]. - Role handling and message normalization (src/api/openai_compat/message_normalizer.py):   * Map incoming role aliases (eg. "system_message", "assistant_role") to canonical roles {system,user,assistant} and attach a deterministic role precedence when multiple system messages exist.   * Preserve metadata like name and function_call hints. - Tests and docs:   * Add unit and integration tests (tests/compat/test_chat_params.py, tests/compat/test_streaming_resume.py, tests/compat/test_tool_envelope.py) covering corner cases: overlapping stop tokens, empty-stop vs null-stop, logprobs+stream, re-connect resume.   * Add docs page (docs/openai-compatibility.md) detailing the adapter behavior and migration notes. Commits (high-level): - 9a1b2c7: initial adapter and param normalization implementation - 3f4d88e: streaming framing and finalization handshake - b12e5f1: tool-call structured envelope and proto definitions - 7d2a90b: tests for stop/logprobs and resume semantics - f8c3a44: docs and examples, example client for streaming resume Checklist: - [x] Param normalization with clear precedence rules - [x] Streaming envelope with finalization chunk - [x] Structured tool_call envelope + human-rendered fallback - [x] Tests for resume + dedupe - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] CI green Notes on compatibility decisions: - We intentionally map null stop to "no stopper" and empty array to "no stopper"; the common interoperability bug was clients sending stop: [] expecting default stop behavior, so the adapter treats both null and [] as no-op unless explicitly provided. - When both temperature and top_p are present, we follow OpenAI convention: if top_p is provided, it is applied, but temperature still scales sampling; we document exact math in docs/openai-compatibility.md. - For logprobs requested in streaming mode, we include a logprob frame in the streaming envelope with token-level logprobs; this increases stream size slightly but matches expectations for tools that compute token-level scoring in real time. Files changed (high-level): - src/api/openai_compat/chat_adapter.py (+210/+46) - src/api/openai_compat/message_normalizer.py (+86/+12) - src/api/openai_compat/tool_call_adapter.py (+124/+8) - src/runtime/stream/framer.py (+142/+30) - pkg/protocol/structured_output.proto (+38/+0) - tests/compat/test_chat_params.py (+210/+14) - tests/compat/test_streaming_resume.py (+132/+18) - docs/openai-compatibility.md (+320/+0) CI summary: initial CI run had lint failures on proto formatting, fixed in commit b12e5f1; final run: all checks passed (unit/integration/e2e). Migration guidance (short): - Existing customers that rely on free-form tool JSON in assistant content will continue to work because we include a rendered fallback at content.rendered, but prefer parsing the stable content.tool_call envelope. - If you previously used stop: [] as a sentinel, audit prompts: adapter now treats [] as no-op. - Streaming clients should be updated to handle framing fields (seq, partial_token, offset) — SDKs will be updated in a follow-up PR to expose a streaming iterator that hides framing. Merge: squashed and merged to main, merge commit 5a7cde1.
release_notes: Normalization of /v1/chat.completions params (temperature/top_p/stop), stable streaming framing with resume/dedupe, structured tool_call envelope, and role/message normalization. Backwards-compatible fallbacks included.
